content:
After an extended period of developer and public beta testing, Apple has officially released macOS 26.6 to all compatible Mac users. Here's what this update includes.

macOS 26.6 Officially Released

macOS 26.6 has been officially released. In addition to patching over 150 security vulnerabilities, it also includes multiple bug fixes and performance improvements. These include correcting the erroneous display of deprecation notices for some Intel-only processor applications, as well as fixing issues affecting HDR screenshots in HealthKit and Messages.

For users preparing to upgrade to macOS 27 Golden Gate later this year, macOS 26.6 has likely already begun indexing work for the new Siri AI, the new version of the Siri App, and other features related to the next generation of Apple Intelligence.

Apple has so far only confirmed this approach for iOS 26.6 and iPadOS 26.6, but it appears the Mac platform will do the same. As users currently running the macOS 27 beta are aware, the indexing process can take several days, so starting early will help reduce the wait time after upgrading later.

The official release version of macOS 26.6 is build 25G72, which differs from last week's release candidate (25G70).

Have you found any new features in macOS 26.6? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
